title: Victoria Sponge
subtitle: Classic British sandwich cake with jam and cream
excerpt: Two light, buttery sponge cakes sandwiched with strawberry jam and freshly whipped cream. The definitive British layer cake, as simple as it is reliable.

recipe.sourceNotes: The Victoria sponge is named in honour of Queen Victoria, who was said to enjoy a slice with her afternoon tea. The cake became popular during the Victorian era as baking powder became widely available, making the reliable rise of a sponge accessible to home bakers without the labour of beating in air by hand for extended periods. The cake is a creamed sponge: butter and sugar are beaten together until very light and fluffy, then eggs and flour are added. The result is a fine-crumbed, moist sponge that is more stable than a whisked sponge and easier to make. The traditional filling is strawberry jam and whipped cream, with icing sugar dusted over the top. No buttercream, no fondant: the Victoria sponge is defined by its restraint. The Women's Institute considers it the benchmark of baking skill and uses it as a competition standard: the ideal Victoria sponge should rise evenly, with a flat, un-cracked top and a soft crumb.

recipeTools.notes: Two 20 cm round loose-bottomed sandwich tins, greased and base-lined.

content.text: All ingredients must be at room temperature: cold butter will not cream properly, and cold eggs can curdle the batter. Cream the butter and sugar until very pale and almost white, at least 4 minutes with an electric whisk. Add the eggs one at a time and beat well between each addition. If the mixture begins to curdle, add a tablespoon of flour with each egg. Fold in the flour with a large metal spoon rather than beating: overworking the flour after adding it makes the sponge tough.

items.preparation: room temperature, plus extra for the tins

content.text: Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease two 20 cm sandwich tins and line the bases with baking parchment. Beat the butter and sugar together for 4 to 5 minutes until very pale and fluffy. Add the vanilla. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well between each addition.

Fold in the sifted flour in two additions using a large metal spoon. Divide the mixture evenly between the two tins and level the surfaces. Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden, risen, and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 5 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack.
Once completely cold, place one sponge on a serving plate. Spread with the strawberry jam. Spoon or pipe the whipped cream over the jam. Place the second sponge on top. Dust with icing sugar.
